translation:
Bhoja Gurjarno Uddhar

_dvapare atha yuge prapte, bhojo pretatvam apsyati ||_
_lilaganena krishnasya, pretamuktir bhavishyati ||1||_
(When the Dvapar age arrives, Bhojo will attain the state of a ghost (pret); and through the singing — kirtan — of Krishna's leela, he will be freed from that ghost-state.)

In Vraj bhoomi there lived an Ahir (cowherd) named Bhoj Gurjar, who had a daughter named Dhanbai. Once, while going to Mathura to sell curd, as the child Krishna was looting the curd, she kept saying no, no — yet he embraced her and kissed her. In this pulling and tugging her garment tore, and a tooth-mark was left on her lower lip. Seeing this, Bhoj Gurjar perceived a fault in it; therefore Shri Krishna, seeing that Bhoj Gurjar had found this fault, cursed him to go into pretyoni (ghost-existence). Having attained the ghost-state in the Dvapar age, Bhoja's ghost entered the body of Rambai, wife of the goldsmith Keshavdas Zadeshwariya of Mangaleshwar. To free this Bhoja from the ghost-existence, Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj — the very form of Shri Krishna — came to Mangaleshwar together with a company of saints on the 2nd day of the bright fortnight of Magsar, Samvat 1716. The account of this event, as a noteworthy record taken down by a Ram Sanehi saint, appears on a page of handwritten manuscript no. 98, and it reads as follows.

In the Dvapar age, Krishna's avatar took place in Gokul; in that, all are devotees (bhakt). Vaishnav Jivandasji too belongs to that same leela (divine play). In the year Samvat 1716, on the 2nd day of the bright fortnight of Magsar, Vaishnav Jivandasji came to the village of Mangaleshwar on the bank of the Narmada; on the way he recited this couplet (sakhi):

_dasho dish bandhu jivana | deu raghupatiki aan ||_
_vaat ghaat raksha kare | chhodve chare khaan ||2||_
(Jivana binds the ten directions, swearing by the name of Raghupati [Ram]; he guards the pathways and river-crossings, and frees [beings] from the four wombs of birth.)

Returning, he came to the village of Mangaleshwar and for many days gave joy to the Vaishnavs. On the 2nd day of the bright fortnight of Jeth, Samvat 1716, Bhoja Gurjar came before Vaishnav Jivandasji and made his plea (a petition) there. He tells of the leela that took place at the time of Krishna's avatar in the Dvapar age. Vaishnav Jivandasji, in the form of a devotee, had been present in Gokul at the time of the raas-leela — it is that event that Bhoja Gurjar describes. Bhoja Gurjar's daughter, named Dhanbai, was at one time attending upon Vaishnav Jivandasji in service; seeing this, her father Bhoja Gurjar took it amiss, and an evil eye/suspicion arose in him. Therefore Krishna cursed Bhoja Gurjar, saying his after-death state would be wretched. Thereafter, when his life ended — that is, when he died — Bhoja Gurjar's wretched state (avagati) came upon him. Afflicted by the suffering of that wretched state, Bhoja Gurjar pleaded with Shri Krishna: "O Maharaj! Why such a thing? I am indeed your servant." Then Shri Krishna said: "You saw fault in My own devotee — that is why this state has befallen you." Then Bhoja Gurjar pleaded for grace. Vaishnav Jivandasji asked him to prove his identity, saying, "How can this be believed?" Then Bhoja Gurjar told of the matter of Brahma — that Brahma had once come to receive prasad but had not received it. He further told another private matter, of the circle of childhood cowherd-friends, saying he would name the cowherds: Arjan, Bhoj, Vishal, Sajal, Gang — and he told their private affairs as well. "Among these, I am Bhoja Gurjar — that is my name" — this is the leela of Gokul that he related. Hearing this, Vaishnav Jivandasji was pleased. He then asked Bhoja whether he would take prasad. Bhoja Gurjar said, "Yes, Maharaj, I will take prasad." Then Vaishnav Jivandasji gave the order that prasad be given to Bhoja. At this time,

Raghukahanji's mother, Bahenjibai, sang a kirtan composed by Narsinh Mehtaji, which has been recorded as follows.
Raag Kolero (Kedaro)

_mathurama mahi vechavane gayan tan, kahanaji'e palav zalyo re ||_
_ma ma karatan alingan didhun, chumban lidhun banh vali re || tek ||_
_aa joni adhar dank lagyo, aa su kidhun anyai re ||_
_bhoja gujar tani re hun beti, marun naam dhanai re ||1||_
_ughadi jaat ahir hamari, bol kuhuna nav sankhu re ||_
_patine gamtan vaar na laage, laaj tamari rakhu re ||2||_
_dahiyan mahiyan vechine jivun, dithade maarag jaau re ||_
_bese kar te kansne aapu, javaab kaho ne na deu re ||3||_
_mara kulmaan kaaval nahotun, mari ratansi dehahi vansai re ||_
_narasaiya chaa swaamini sange ramtaan, sansaar vaat jaanavi re ||4||_
(We had gone to Mathura to sell curd; on the way, Shri Krishna caught hold of the end of my sari-hem. I said no, no, and still he embraced me, held me tight in his arms, and kissed me. But from this a tooth-mark was left on my lower lip — ah, what an improper thing you have done! I am the daughter of Bhoja Gurjar; my name is Dhanbai. We of the cowherd caste are of such a shameless, brazen nature that we heed no one's disgrace; I never tolerate anyone's ill jest or ill word. Though it takes no time to become displeasing to one's husband, still I guard your honor. I walk only my own familiar path, and I make my living selling curd and butter; whatever toll falls due I pay to Kansa, and to no one besides him do I give anything. There was not the least stain of misconduct in my family, but in this way you have defiled my pure body. In sporting with Shri Krishna, whom Narsinh Mehta worships, this matter of mine has become known to the whole world.)

Then Vaishnav Jivandasji said: "Are you that Bhoja? And is this Dhanbai?" Bhoja Gurjar replied: "Yes, Maharaj, I am that Bhoja, and this is Dhanbai." Then Vaishnavji accepted the matter as true. Vaishnav Jivandasji then said: "Bhoja, what fault has Dhanbai committed?" He then asked Bhoja: "Which prasad will you take?" Bhoja Gurjar answered: "O Maharaj! In the way we used to play the chhakleeli (curd-sport) in Gokul, give me the prasad of curd in that same manner." Then Vaishnav Jivandasji told Harmabai to bring the gauras (curds). Harmaba brought the curds. At that time Gopaldas told Naranadas and Vasantdas to fetch a padiyo (leaf-cup). As Vasantdas rose to fetch the leaf-cup, Vaishnav Jivandasji asked: "O Bhoja! In what will you take the prasad?" Bhoja Gurjar said: "O Maharaj! In the way we used to take it there in Gokul, I will take it cupped in the hollow of my palm." So Vasantdas, who was going to fetch the leaf-cup, turned back. Then the curd prasad was given to Bhoja, and Bhoja received it in his palm. After that Bhoja Gurjar said, "Now I am satisfied." Bhoja Gurjar then asked leave to depart, pleading: "O Maharaj! Remove all my faults." Vaishnav Jivandasji then said: "O Bhoja, whatever faults you have had, past and present, up to this day — the Gracious Lord (Kripanath) has removed them all." Bhoja Gurjar then bowed in reverence, and as soon as he bowed, Bhoja Gurjar's deliverance (uddhar) took place, and he reached the presence of Kripanath. This account has become known from a handwritten manuscript, written by the Ram Sanehi sadhu Bilasi Ram — disciple of Guru Duleramji — on Chaitra Vad 10, Vikram Samvat 1872, and obtained from Vaishnav Dasalad Prabhu Mangalji.

Bhoja Gurjar, cupping his palms as a leaf-bowl, expressed the wish to drink in the very manner he had once drunk curd-milk among the company of cowherds in Vrindavan. Having lived a span as long as five thousand years, from the Dvapar age down to this day in Kaliyug, his deliverance came about; regarding this, the devotee Dayaldas has written a pad (hymn):

_bhoja gujarne odhaariyo, mangaleshwar mozhaar |_
_paanch sahasra varsha rahyo pret jonaman, paayo dukh apaar ||_
(Bhoja Gurjar was delivered, in the midst of Mangaleshwar; he remained five thousand years in the ghost-existence, and endured boundless suffering.)

To deliver Bhoja Gurjar, who had endured the ghost-existence for five thousand years, Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj had to come — because when Shri Krishna cursed him, he had said: "The very one whose faults you have seen — that same one shall deliver you."

Among Sadguru Jivanji Maharaj's most exalted devotees, in the women's line, were Bhagat Raghubhai of Kandari and Bahenjibai, mother of Kahandas. The pad composed by Narsinh Mehta relating to Bhoja Gurjar — "We had gone to Mathura to sell curd" — this she sang. Now, Narsinh Mehta lived before Jivanji Maharaj's time, so the doubt may arise that this pad could not be Narsinh Mehta's own; but Narsinh Mehta also composed a pad relating to Jivanji Maharaj, one that mentions Dhanbai by name, in his own collected Harmala (garland of hymns) — there is another such pad. This pad appears, in this form, in Bhagat Bapu Vrindavan Patrawala's book no. 1, page 48, and in Bhagat Ranchhod Haribhai Vayada Polwala's book, page 240.

_vahalo gokulman raheto, tahan navneet chori leto ||_
_gurjari dhanai gher jaato, tahan taadho toomro khaato ||1||_
_dhanai baandhati gaanthe taani, tahan mukaavta saarangpaani ||_
_tamo te vela sambhalo, ehavun jaanine ugaaro ||2||_
_maaho maahe motaai na aano, mune potaano kari jaano ||_
_maahari pat jaataan taahaari jaase, tyaare vaikunthaman nahin rahevaas ||3||_
_am sanghaate vaad na kije, mune haar taantano dije ||_
_lok varvaan bole maaharaan, dhaank maaharaan udhaadis taaharaan ||4||_
_hala maahara roode taaharun roodun, maahare bhoonde taaharun bhoondun ||_
_naagar batka bola kahiye, tun to kaain na aane haiye ||5||_
_ha tun kohona roodeman betho, valti maahaari mite nahin ditho ||_
_tune vrukhabhaan suta rahi raakhi, tene aanandthi joto zhaankhi, ehavi ved vade chhe saakhi ||6||_
_shukdev naarde chhupaayo, parikshitne shravane samaao ||_
_pretne mukti to param vallabh, hetuna jiv te hetu trute ||7||_
_taare narasaiyo rise bharaay, muj vina jash kon gaay ||_
_taahara varvaan pooraan na thaae, pad ek narasaiyo gaay ||8||_
(The Beloved of the people of Braj, Shri Krishna, when he dwelt in Vraj, used to steal butter there. He would go always to the house of Dhanbai, the Gurjar cowherd-woman, and eat there the cold, coarse millet-porridge she offered. When Dhanbai bound it up and tied it away in her provision-bundle, the Lord would break it free from her by force — so remember that leela of that time, and knowing that you were once such a one, deliver us from illusion (maya). Do not, between us, keep any difference or discrimination; make me truly your own — your maidservant, your servant. If my honor is lost, your own honor will be lost too; then in Vaikunth you will grow restless to save me, and you will come running from there to my rescue, unable to remain at rest in Vaikunth. So rather than that, you ought not to bandy words or delay with us; give me some slight help, like a slender thread's worth, for people speak ill of me. If you do not protect my honor, I will not sing your praises, but will instead make your weakness known... Ah, in my well-being is your own well-being; in my misfortune, your honor too will be lost. A person as plain-speaking as I will surely say that in your heart you hold no true feeling for us. Ah — in whose heart have you settled, that even my keen eye has failed to catch sight of you again? Surely Vrishabhanu's daughter Radha keeps you bound in some illicit relation, and you too, they say — those who know the Vedas — secretly watch her with sweet, loving glances. Such leela of yours with Radha, Shukdev and Narad kept concealed, and told Parikshit other things instead. For a ghost (pret), to hear even harsh things said, if it brings about deliverance, is welcomed gladly — for such deliverance is most dear to it. Self-interested souls become content the moment their own purpose is served. That is why, whenever such concealment happens, Narsinh Mehta grows displeased with you. Yet without me, who will sing your praise and glory? Your faults cannot fully be told, but this Narsinh sings this one hymn of yours.)

In this pad, the ghost-turned character of the Bhagavat, Gokarna, had only the self-interest that his own deliverance would come about through hearing the Bhagavat recited. But the ghost-turned Bhoja has the aspiration of being freed from the ghost-existence and reaching the abode of Kripanath.

That Narsinh Mehta composed this poem with reference to Dhanbai proves that Narsinh Mehta had full knowledge of such matters of Krishna's leela. Furthermore, in the 94th pad of the Harmala too, there is mention of Dhanbai.

Raag – Prabhati

_mahare mandalik su padi chhe hod re, mune tahara charan joyana kod re |_
_mune bhav bandhanthi chhod re, tamo zakh maarso mune haar aapso || tek ||_
_mune tamo vecho tahan vechau re, kaache taantane bandhai jaau re |_
_hun govindana gun gaau re ... ... ... ... ||1||_
_tune gurjar dhanai bandhati ghaado tani re, taare hun mukaavto saarangpani re |_
_men to pothanmata tahaari jaani re, tento maahari poorav preet na jaani re ||2||_
_lok varvan bole chhe maharan re, dhaankya maharan ke ughades tahaaran re |_
_tahaaran manda haju nathi hariyaan re, ... ... ... ... ||3||_
_tune vrushabhaan suta rahi chhe raakhi re, te to maahara manman rahyo chhun saankhi re |_
_men karuna tahari bhaakhi re, ... ... ... ... ||4||_
_amo naagar batak bola kahiye, kahyaan kathan na aaniye haiye re |_
_tam vina sharane amo kohone rahiye re, ... ... ... ||5||_
_tahaaro narasaiyo rose bharaay re, muj vina jas tahara kon gaay re |_
_tun van vaahare maahaari kon dhaay re, ... ... ... ... ||6||_
(I have made a wager for victory or defeat with King Mandalik; I long only to behold your feet. Free me from the bondage of worldly existence, and — even reluctantly, only when there is no other way — come to that place and grant me victory. If you were to sell me, I would let myself be sold — whatever wretched state you put me in, I would accept it, and rather than act willfully toward you, I shall remain faithful to you; and I shall sing the praises of the Lord.
